name: פתיחת סוגריים – מכפלת שלושה גורמים בשלושה משתנים (באנגלית)
questiontext:
Expand the following:

\(\left({{CT:0}}\right)\left({{CT:1}}\right)\left({{CT:2}}\right)\) = [[input:ans]]
[[validation:ans]]
generalfeedback:
Outline: When multiplying out 3 brackets the best thing to do is focus on 2 brackets at a time: multiply out \(\left({{CT:1}}\right)\left({{CT:2}}\right)\) first, putting \(\left( {{CT:0}} \right)\) to the side for the time being.
Step 1 — Multiply the last two brackets
Each term of the first bracket times each term of the second:

\[ \left({{CT:1}}\right)\left({{CT:2}}\right)=\left({{CT:3}}\right)\left({{CT:4}}\right)+\left({{CT:3}}\right)\left(-x\right)+\left(-z\right)\left({{CT:4}}\right)+\left(-z\right)\left(-x\right)={{CT:5}} \]

So

\[ {{CT:6}}. \]

Step 2 — Multiply by the remaining bracket
Multiply every term of the four-term bracket by \({{CT:7}}\) and by \(-y\):

\[ {{CT:7}}\cdot\left({{CT:5}}\right)={{CT:8}} \]

\[ -y\cdot\left({{CT:5}}\right)={{CT:9}} \]

Step 3 — Collect like terms
Add the two results; the only like terms are the two terms in \(xyz\):

\[ {{CT:10}}. \]

on_true.feedback: Your answer is algebraically equivalent to the correct answer but you need to leave the answer as a polynomial (multiply out the brackets!)
